title: Shape the Minecraft Launcher
question: Which layout should carry forward? Each preview shows the same stopped-server example. These are static design mockups; selecting one approves a layout, not an implementation.

options.label: Ready to play
options.thesis: A clear server-readiness stage leads into device-specific joining help.
options.viewport: A broad status-and-start area, followed by Java, Bedrock and console guidance.
options.risk: The larger readiness area takes more room before the connection details.

options.label: Quick launch
options.thesis: A compact status-and-start strip keeps the joining guide close at hand.
options.viewport: Server name, status and Start server share one row above the device guide.
options.risk: A compact status can be easier for a first-time player to overlook.

options.label: Status beside setup
options.thesis: Keep server readiness visible alongside the connection steps.
options.viewport: A narrow status column sits beside a larger device-selection and joining area.
options.risk: The split must become one clear sequence on a phone.
